title: Article 5 — Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution

content.overview: Article 5 determines who became a citizen of India at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950). A person who had domicile in the territory of India and who satisfied any one of three alternative conditions (birth in India, parent born in India, or ordinary residence for not less than five years immediately preceding commencement) became a citizen.
content.glance: At commencement: domicile in India + (birth in India OR parent born in India OR 5 years ordinary residence) → citizen.
content.study:
Article 5 (Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution):

At the commencement of this Constitution every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and—
(a) who was born in the territory of India; or
(b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India; or
(c) who has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding such commencement,
shall be a citizen of India.

Structure: domicile is the base condition; any one of (a), (b) or (c) is sufficient.

Domicile: used in the private-international-law sense of permanent home; it is a question of fact and intention.

Articles 5–8 together fixed the initial body of citizens at commencement. Articles 9–11 then deal with loss, continuance and Parliament’s ongoing regulatory power. Modern acquisition, termination and related rules are primarily in the Citizenship Act, 1955 (as amended), enacted under Article 11.

Examination focus: quote the three alternative limbs; emphasise domicile as the common requirement; distinguish commencement citizenship (Arts 5–8) from post-commencement statutory citizenship (Citizenship Act under Art 11).

sections.heading: Constitutional text
sections.body:
At the commencement of this Constitution every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and—
(a) who was born in the territory of India; or
(b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India; or
(c) who has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding such commencement,
shall be a citizen of India.

sections.heading: Ingredients
sections.body:
1. Domicile in the territory of India at commencement (mandatory).
2. Plus any one of:
   (a) birth in the territory of India; or
   (b) either parent born in the territory of India; or
   (c) ordinary residence in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding commencement.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Commencement date: 26 January 1950.
2. Domicile + one of three alternatives.
3. Articles 5–8 = initial citizens; Article 11 + Citizenship Act 1955 = ongoing regulation.
4. Do not treat Article 5 as a continuing mode of acquisition after commencement.

examples.title: Illustration — Ordinary residence limb
examples.body: A person domiciled in India on 26 January 1950 who was not born in India and whose parents were not born in India, but who had been ordinarily resident in India for six years immediately before commencement, became a citizen under Article 5(c).

misconceptions.trap: Article 5 is still the primary mode of acquiring Indian citizenship today.
misconceptions.correction: Article 5 fixed citizenship at commencement. Post-commencement acquisition and termination are governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955, enacted under Article 11.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who became a citizen of India under Article 5?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 5, every person who at the commencement of the Constitution had domicile in the territory of India and who (a) was born in the territory of India, or (b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India, or (c) had been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding commencement, became a citizen of India.

examTips: Memorise: domicile + (birth / parent birth / 5 years residence). Link to Art 11 for modern law.

keyTakeaways: Art 5: domicile + birth / parental birth / 5 years residence at commencement.
Commencement citizenship only; ongoing regulation under Art 11 + Citizenship Act.
